grammar.title: Vます — polite verbs: present, negative, past
grammar.pattern: Vます / Vません / Vました / Vませんでした
grammar.meaning: do (will do) / don't (won't) / did / didn't — polite
grammar.explanation: Japanese verbs always come at the very end of the sentence, and in polite speech they end in ます. The ます form covers both habits and the future: 食べます means "I eat" or "I will eat". Swap the ending to get the other forms: ません (don't / won't), ました (did), ませんでした (didn't). The word list shows verbs in their dictionary form (食べる, 行く); for now, just learn each verb's ます form together with it.
notes: Present ます is also the future: 明日行きます = I'll go tomorrow.
Irregular: する → します, 来る (くる) → 来ます (きます).
The subject is usually dropped: 食べました alone = I ate.

grammar.title: を — object marker
grammar.meaning: marks the thing the action is done to
grammar.explanation: を marks the direct object — the thing you eat, drink, watch, read and so on. It comes right after that noun, and the verb follows: パンを食べます = I eat bread. を has its own hiragana, but it is pronounced just like お ("o"). Verbs like 食べる, 飲む, 見る, 読む and 聞く almost always come with を.
notes: を is pronounced "o".
Noun + する verbs can also take を: 勉強をします = 勉強します.
Don't use を for places you go to — that's へ / に.

grammar.title: に — at a point in time
grammar.explanation: Put に after a specific time to say when something happens: 七時に起きます = I get up at seven. Use に with clock times and days of the week. Do NOT use に with relative time words such as 今日, 明日, 昨日, 毎日 or 来週 — they stand on their own. Words like 朝 (morning) and 夜 (night) also usually go without に.
notes: With に: 六時に, 月曜日に.
Without に: 今日, 明日, 昨日, 今朝, 毎朝, 来週, いつ.
Ask "what time?": 何時に起きますか。

grammar.title: へ / に — going to a place
grammar.pattern: Place へ / に 行きます・来ます・帰ります
grammar.explanation: With verbs of movement — 行きます (go), 来ます (come) and 帰ります (go home, return) — mark the destination with へ or に. Both mean "to" here: へ stresses the direction and に the arrival point, but in everyday speech you can use either. The particle へ is written with the hiragana へ but pronounced "e". Ask where someone is going with どこへ行きますか.
notes: へ is pronounced "e".
帰ります means going back to where you belong — home, or your own country.
Going nowhere: どこへも行きません。

grammar.title: で — where an action happens (and by what means)
grammar.pattern: Place で V / Transport で 行きます
grammar.meaning: at / in (place of an activity); by (means)
grammar.explanation: で marks the place where an action happens: 図書館で勉強します = I study at the library. Compare へ / に, which mark where you are going to. If you DO something at a place — eat, study, work, watch — use で. で also marks the means you use, such as transport: 電車で行きます = I go by train.
notes: で = at (doing something there); へ = to (moving there).
Transport: 電車で, バスで, 自転車で. On foot is 歩いて — no で.
Ask where: どこで食べますか。

grammar.title: と — with (someone)
grammar.explanation: と after a person means "with": 友だちと映画を見ます = I watch a movie with a friend. You can add 一緒に (together) after it for emphasis: 友だちと一緒に. Ask who someone is doing something with by putting と after だれ: だれと行きますか. If you do something alone, say ひとりで instead — no と.
notes: 友だちと一緒に = together with a friend.
だれと行きますか。 = Who are you going with?
と also joins nouns ("A and B") — you'll meet that in Unit 5.

grammar.title: Vませんか / Vましょう — inviting and "let's"
grammar.pattern: Vませんか / Vましょう
grammar.explanation: To invite someone politely, use the negative question ませんか: 一緒に行きませんか literally means "won't you go with me?" and works like "would you like to go together?". It sounds gentle because it leaves room to say no. ましょう means "let's": 行きましょう = Let's go. A typical exchange is an invitation with ませんか and an answer with ましょう.
notes: ませんか = polite invitation; ましょう = let's (also used to accept).
Accepting: ええ、いいですね。 Declining gently: すみません、ちょっと…
ましょうか = shall we…?: 何時に会いましょうか。

reading.title: わたしの まいにち — My daily routine
reading.text: 私[わたし]は会社員[かいしゃいん]です。毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]に起[お]きます。家[うち]でパンを食[た]べます。コーヒーも飲[の]みます。七時半[しちじはん]に電車[でんしゃ]で会社[かいしゃ]へ行[い]きます。仕事[しごと]は九時[くじ]から六時[ろくじ]までです。十二時[じゅうにじ]に友[とも]だちと昼[ひる]ごはんを食[た]べます。夜[よる]は家[うち]でテレビを見[み]ます。十一時[じゅういちじ]に寝[ね]ます。週末[しゅうまつ]は働[はたら]きません。今日[きょう]は土曜日[どようび]です。午後[ごご]、友[とも]だちと映画[えいが]を見[み]ます。明日[あした]は家[うち]で休[やす]みます。
reading.en: I'm a company employee. I get up at six every morning. I eat bread at home. I drink coffee too. At seven thirty I go to the office by train. Work is from nine to six. At twelve I eat lunch with a friend. In the evening I watch TV at home. I go to bed at eleven. I don't work at weekends. Today is Saturday. In the afternoon I'm going to see a movie with a friend. Tomorrow I'll rest at home.
